userStories.title: Configure the koda memory provider
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the optional koda schema, runtime types, validation and public config exports.

**Motivation** — The user ruled (2026-11-02) that nax chat and koda threads share ONE memory with koda as the source of truth, and that nax pulls a per-project mirror (pull architecture, design 6.5).

**Approach** — `MemoryKodaConfigSchema` (new, in `src/config/schemas-memory.ts`) is `.strict()`: `url` is an optional `https:` URL, or an `http:` URL to a loopback host (the existing `isRemotePlainHttp`, `src/config/schemas-model.ts:184`, decides; a remote plain-http url fails with the message `memory.koda.url must use https unless the host is loopback`, because the bearer key travels with every request); `project` is an optional string matching `KODA_PROJECT_SLUG_RE` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,99}$`, koda's slug rule); `headers` is an optional record of strings defaulting to `{}`. `memory.provider` accepts `"local" | "mcp" | "koda"`. `memory.koda` has no default and is absent from `NaxConfigSchema.parse({}).memory`. The file's header comment, which says `koda` is rejected until this feature, is updated.

New cross-section rules in `validateMemoryProvider`:

| Condition | Issue path | Message |
|---|---|---|
| `memory.provider` is `"koda"` and `memory.koda.url` is absent | `["memory", "koda", "url"]` | `memory.provider "koda" needs memory.koda.url in ~/.nax/config.json` |
| `memory.provider` is `"koda"` and `memory.koda.project` is absent | `["memory", "koda", "project"]` | `memory.provider "koda" needs memory.koda.project (run nax memory link <koda-project>)` |

Proposal write mode is allowed with `"koda"` (koda holds pending writes).

The `@/config` barrel (`src/config/index.ts`) also exports `KODA_PROJECT_SLUG_RE`, `MemoryKodaConfigSchema` and the type `MemoryKodaConfig`, beside the existing memory exports.

`MemoryConfigSchema.provider` — Target: `z.enum(["local", "mcp", "koda"]).default("local")`, plus `koda: MemoryKodaConfigSchema.optional()`. `validateMemoryProvider(data, ctx)` — Target: the four MCP rules plus the two koda rules above; `MemoryProviderInput.memory` gains `koda?: { url?: string; project?: string }`.

Replace the two existing tests asserting that koda fails at the provider enum with acceptance of a complete koda configuration and missing-url validation of an incomplete one. Keep existing local/MCP defaults, strictness and validation behavior.

**Scope** — In: schemas-memory.ts, runtime-types-memory.ts, config barrel and existing schema tests. Out: global-only layer enforcement and descriptions (US-012), HTTP client (US-002), provider and host composition (US-005–US-009). Credential sources for `memory.koda.headers` other than literal values: no `${VAR}` expansion and no `auth`/exec credential source.

**Interface** —
```typescript
export const KODA_PROJECT_SLUG_RE = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,99}$/;
```
`MemoryKodaConfig = { url?: string; project?: string; headers: Record<string, string> }`. `MemoryConfig.provider` becomes `"local" | "mcp" | "koda"`, and gains `koda?: MemoryKodaConfig`.

userStories.title: Implement koda reachability and save delivery
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Create the koda provider with identity, reachability, cached project-id lookup and direct/proposal saves.

**Motivation** — The provider seam, the outbox and the sync loop were built for exactly this provider; `local` never exercises a remote cursor and `mcp` has none, so this is also the first provider that pulls.

**Approach** — `memory.provider: "koda"` makes the host compose a koda provider for the koda project named by `memory.koda.project`. The mirror stays the store every surface reads; the index, `get` and local keyword search are unchanged. koda's wire contract (verified against koda `c51cf74e`):

- every path is relative to `memory.koda.url`, the API root including koda's global prefix (`https://koda.example/api`);
- authentication is the configured headers, normally `Authorization: Bearer <agent key>`. The agent needs a project role carrying `project.read` (for `GET projects/<slug>`), `memory.read` and `memory.create`; superseding or retiring a row another principal owns also needs `memory.update`;
- a success body is `{ "ret": 0, "data": <payload> }`; an error body is `{ "ret": <code>, "message": "<text>" }`;
- routes address the project by **slug** in the path; `POST memory` and the retire body take the project **id**, which the provider learns once from `GET projects/<slug>`.

`reachable` — `GET projects/<slug>/memory/write-mode`; `true` on a 2xx whose `data.mode` is `"direct"` or `"proposal"`, `false` otherwise (a throw included). It checks the key and the membership, which `GET health` would not.

`push` save — `POST memory` with the body below; `201` resolves `{ id: <koda id>, status: "active" }`; `202` records the approval and resolves `{ id: <clientId>, status: "pending" }`.

The provider id is `koda:<project>`, so `nax memory status` prints `provider: koda:rs-stock`.

**Write mode is koda's.** koda decides direct vs proposal from its own approval policy for the calling agent; the request's `writeMode` is not sent. A `201` is active and a `202` is pending whatever `memory.writeMode` says locally. `memory.writeMode` keeps its existing local meaning (how an offline save is marked while it waits in the outbox).

**Idempotency.** koda has no client idempotency key. The save carries `sourceId: <clientId>`: koda returns the existing row for an identical restatement (same object, predicate, description, sourceType and sourceId), so re-pushing a queued entry whose first answer was lost does not create a second row. A note's koda id changes on every content change (supersession), which is why the mirror stays keyed by scope and slug.

### Save request body (the wire shape)
```json
{
  "projectId": "<koda project id from GET projects/<slug>>",
  "kind": "NOTE",
  "subject": "<slug>",
  "predicate": "<type: user | feedback | project | reference>",
  "object": "<body>",
  "description": "<description>",
  "scope": "<project | user>",
  "sourceType": "<note.source, e.g. nax-chat>",
  "sourceId": "<clientId>"
}
```
Every key is always present, with exactly these names. `projectId` is sent for user-scope notes too (koda requires it for membership). No other key is sent.

### Error classification (provider)
| Answer | save |
|---|---|
| `400`, `403`, `413`, `422` | `MEMORY_PUSH_REJECTED` with koda's message |
| `409` | `MEMORY_PUSH_REJECTED` |
| `404` | rethrown (transient: a wrong slug or lost membership is a config problem; the entry stays queued) |
| `401`, `408`, `429`, `5xx`, timeout, unreachable, bad response | rethrown (transient) |

`403` is permanent for a write: koda refuses a principal that lacks `memory.create`, or lacks `memory.update` on another principal's row, and the drain stops at the first transient failure, so a transient `403` would block every later write. A rejected entry is retried by the user through the outbox's existing rejected-entry handling. `401` (a bad key) stays transient: fixing the key delivers everything queued. Any failure of the forget lookup itself is transient.

`GET projects/<slug>` answer without a string `data.id` → `MEMORY_KODA_BAD_RESPONSE`; the project id is not memoised.

US-005 creates `koda-provider.ts` with `pull` resolving `{ notes: [], done: true }` and `search` resolving `[]`; US-006 replaces `search` and adds the forget; US-007 replaces `pull` with a call to `pullKodaPage`; US-008 adds proposal resolution to `pullKodaPage`. Tests drive the provider over a real createKodaClient with _kodaClientDeps.fetch stubbed and real createKodaApprovals in a temporary directory; assert requests and recorded file.

**Scope** — In: provider shell, project-id memoisation, reachable, save delivery, 202 recording and error classification. Out: forget/search (US-006), pull (US-007), proposal resolution (US-008), host composition (US-009). Retries or backoff inside the provider: a transient failure leaves the entry in the outbox for the next sync. A degraded mode for a koda older than `c51cf74e`: the provider needs koda #376-#379 deployed; an older koda answers `400` to a `NOTE` save and the outbox marks it rejected. De-duplicating koda approval requests when a `202` save is re-pushed because its first answer was lost.

**Interface** —
```typescript
export const MEMORY_KODA_PROVIDER_PREFIX = "koda:";
export const MEMORY_KODA_APPROVAL_CHECKS_MAX = 20;
export interface CreateKodaMemoryProviderInput {
  readonly client: KodaClient;
  readonly project: string;                                   // koda project slug
  readonly approvals: KodaApprovals;
  readonly readNote: (scope: MemoryScope, slug: string) => Promise<MemoryNote | null>;
  readonly readDecisions: () => Promise<readonly MemoryDecision[]>;
  readonly logger: MemoryLogger;
}
export function createKodaMemoryProvider(input: CreateKodaMemoryProviderInput): MemoryProvider;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] createKodaMemoryProvider({ project: "rs-stock", ... }).id is "koda:rs-stock".

[unit] The POST memory body has exactly the nine keys of the save request body and no writeMode key, also when the request's writeMode is "proposal".
[unit] A user-scope save sends "scope": "user" and the project id.
[unit] Two saves on one provider request GET projects/rs-stock once.
[unit] A GET projects/rs-stock answer without a string data.id rejects the save with MEMORY_KODA_BAD_RESPONSE, and the next save requests the project again.

[unit] A 202 save answer with data.id "apr_1" resolves { id: "c1", status: "pending" }.
[unit] A 202 save answer records { approvalId: "apr_1", scope: "project", slug: "replay-budget", clientId: "c1" } in the provider's approvals.
[unit] A 422 save answer rejects with an error isMemoryPushRejected recognises, whose message includes koda's message.

[unit] A 404 save answer rejects with an error isMemoryPushRejected does not recognise.
[unit] A 503 save answer rejects with an error isMemoryPushRejected does not recognise.
[unit] For save answers 400 and 413, push rejects with MEMORY_PUSH_REJECTED whose message includes koda's message.
[unit] For save answers 408, 429 and other 5xx responses, or timeout, unreachable and bad-response errors, push rethrows a transient error rather than MEMORY_PUSH_REJECTED.
[unit] When the write-mode probe throws because koda is unreachable, rejects the key, or denies project membership, reachable() resolves false.
[integration] When syncMemory drains saves answered 400/403/409/413/422, the outbox marks those entries rejected and continues delivering later queued writes.
[integration] When a save fails transiently with 401/404/408/429/5xx, timeout, unreachable or bad response, syncMemory retains its queued outbox entry and records the error.

routing.reasoning: One provider module follows the existing MCP factory pattern over supplied HTTP and approval interfaces; credentialed reachability and permission-refusal classification still require strict security TDD.

suggestedCriteria: reachable() resolves true when the probe answers data.mode direct.
When a save answers 201 while request.writeMode is proposal, push returns active without recording an approval.
When a save answers 202 while request.writeMode is direct, push returns pending and records its approval.

userStories.title: Deliver forgets and search koda notes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add exact-match paginated lookup, remote retire delivery and full-text search to the provider.

**Motivation** — Today a note saved in nax chat or a `nax run` lives only in one machine's mirror (`local`) or in an MCP server that koda cannot read.

**Approach** — `push` forget — finds the slug's active note (forget lookup, below); none resolves `{ id: <clientId>, status: "deleted" }`; else `POST memory/notes/<id>/retire`: `201` resolves `deleted`, `202` resolves `pending`, `404` and `409` resolve `deleted`.

### Retire request body
`POST memory/notes/<koda id>/retire` with `{ "projectId": "<koda project id>", "reason": "<reason>" }`; `reason` is omitted when the forget's reason is the empty string.

### Forget lookup (`src/memory/koda-lookup.ts`)
`GET projects/<slug>/memory` with query `kind=NOTE`, `subject=<slug>`, `scope=<scope>`, `status=active`, `size=100` and `current=<page>` starting at `1`. A forget runs the lookup first; only when it finds a row does it fetch the project id (`GET projects/<slug>`, memoised) and send the retire. The `404`/`409` → `deleted` mapping applies to the retire request only: a `404` from the lookup or from `GET projects/<slug>` is transient like any other failure of those requests. A forget can cost up to `MEMORY_KODA_LOOKUP_MAX_PAGES` + 2 requests, which may outlast sync's 10 s race; the retry is safe because retiring an already retired note answers `409` → `deleted`. koda's `subject` filter is a prefix match, so the answer is the first record whose `subject` equals the slug exactly and whose `scope` equals the scope. The lookup asks the next page while no record matches and the answer's `data.hasNext` is `true`, up to `MEMORY_KODA_LOOKUP_MAX_PAGES` pages; no match with `hasNext` false resolves `null`; reaching the page cap without a match throws `NaxError` `MEMORY_KODA_LOOKUP_EXHAUSTED` (transient). It is used by the forget and by proposal resolution.

### Error classification (provider)
| Answer | forget (retire) |
|---|---|
| `400`, `403`, `413`, `422` | `MEMORY_PUSH_REJECTED` with koda's message |
| `409` | resolves `deleted` (the note is no longer active) |
| `404` | resolves `deleted` (the note is gone) |
| `401`, `408`, `429`, `5xx`, timeout, unreachable, bad response | rethrown (transient) |

`403` is permanent for a write: koda refuses a principal that lacks `memory.create`, or lacks `memory.update` on another principal's row, and the drain stops at the first transient failure, so a transient `403` would block every later write. A rejected entry is retried by the user through the outbox's existing rejected-entry handling. `401` (a bad key) stays transient: fixing the key delivers everything queued. Any failure of the forget lookup itself is transient.

`search` — `GET projects/<slug>/memory` with `text`, `kind=NOTE` and the scope; records mapped to hits in koda's rank order.

**Hits.** A search record maps to `{ slug: subject, scope: record scope, type: predicate, description, status: "active", score: <records.length - index>, snippet: <object with whitespace runs collapsed, first 200 characters> }`; a record that fails R2 maps to `null` and is dropped. R2: `subject` fails `MEMORY_SLUG_RE`, `predicate` is not one of `user`, `feedback`, `project`, `reference`, or a required field (`id`, `subject`, `predicate`, `object`, `description`, `updatedAt`, `status`) is missing or not a string. Search trims blank text to no request, sends at most the first 100 characters of text, caps size at 100, and cuts mapped hits to the requested limit. The query insertion order is kind, scope, text, size. Add kodaHitOf to the mapping module created by US-003. Test provider search/forget over the real client with injected fetch, asserting request order/body and mapped hits.

**Scope** — In: koda-lookup.ts, kodaHitOf, provider forget/search and operation tests. Out: export pull (US-007), approval resolution (US-008), host search changes. userStories.title: Pull and checkpoint koda export pages
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Implement provider pull through a dedicated export-page adapter with note reconciliation and project decision merging.

**Motivation** — The provider seam, the outbox and the sync loop were built for exactly this provider; `local` never exercises a remote cursor and `mcp` has none, so this is also the first provider that pulls.

**Approach** — `GET projects/<slug>/memory/export` with query `since=<cursor>` (omitted when the cursor is `null`) and `take=<min(take, 500)>`. The answer's `data` is `{ items: KodaMemoryItem[], nextCursor: string | null, hasMore: boolean }`, ordered by `(updatedAt, id)` ascending. Each row appears once, at its latest `updatedAt`: a supersession, retirement or soft delete rewrites the row in place and moves it to the end of the feed. koda withholds rows changed in the last 5 seconds (`MEMORY_EXPORT_SETTLE_MS`), so a write shows up on a later sync. Rows of both scopes arrive in one feed (the project's rows, plus the calling principal's user-scope rows); there is no scope parameter, so a user-scope pull reads the same feed as a project pull and keeps only the user rows. The page answers `{ notes, decisions?, nextCursor: data.nextCursor ?? undefined, done: data.hasMore !== true }`.

The mirror ids R5 compares against are read before the page is reconciled: the provider reads the mirror note of every distinct slug the page's rows of this scope name, through the `readNote` it was given, and passes the ids as a map. Read once for each distinct slug passing R2, as required by the acceptance criterion. Reconcile through reconcileKodaNotes rather than applying raw rows. R2 requires a valid MEMORY_SLUG_RE subject, predicate user/feedback/project/reference, and string id/subject/predicate/object/description/updatedAt/status; R1 ignores non-NOTE or wrong-scope rows. Matching superseded ids make the slug's current id unknown within this page; active rows replace it, and rejected/deleted tombstones apply only to matching or unknown ids. Output at most one note per slug in code-point order.

**Decisions.** `DECISION` rows are merged only on project pages. A `DECISION` row whose `id`, `subject`, `predicate`, `object`, `updatedAt` or `status` is missing or not a string is skipped and counted with the note skips. A page with no valid `DECISION` row answers `decisions` undefined, so `decisions.jsonl` is not rewritten. A page with one or more merges them into the mirror's current decisions (`readDecisions`; sync writes `decisions.jsonl` after each page, so a later page sees the earlier one) by `id`: an `active` row with no `deletedAt` sets `{ id, subject, predicate, object, updatedAt, status: "active" }`; any other row removes its id. The merged list is ordered by `updatedAt` descending then `id`, and cut to `MEMORY_KODA_DECISIONS_MAX` (500). Rows of other kinds (`FACT`, `PREFERENCE`, `CONSTRAINT`, `INCIDENT_PATTERN`) are ignored.

Export answer whose `data.items` is not an array or whose `data.hasMore` is not a boolean → `MEMORY_KODA_BAD_RESPONSE`; sync keeps the last checkpointed cursor. Export row that fails R2, or an invalid `DECISION` row → skipped, counted, logged at warn once per page with the count. Do not call readDecisions for user pages.

US-007 replaces `pull` with a call to `pullKodaPage`; US-008 adds proposal resolution to `pullKodaPage`. The pull is kept out of koda-provider.ts for the 600-line cap. Exercise reconcileKodaNotes and mergeKodaDecisions through a real provider with fetch stubbed, and use syncMemory over a real store for the stale-tombstone integration regression.

**Scope** — In: koda-pull.ts, provider delegation, feed validation and mapping integration tests. Out: resolving proposals (US-008), composing the host (US-009). Any change in `packages/nax-agent`. Mirroring koda memory kinds other than `NOTE` and `DECISION` (`FACT`, `PREFERENCE`, `CONSTRAINT`, `INCIDENT_PATTERN`). Keeping a pending local edit visible while its proposal is open: a pull carrying the slug's unchanged active row replaces it until the approved row arrives. A supersession and a retirement of one note that land on two different export pages: R3/R5 track an unknown current id within one page only, so the stale active note survives until the next change to that slug.

**Interface** —
```typescript
export function pullKodaPage(
  input: CreateKodaMemoryProviderInput,
  request: { readonly scope: MemoryScope; readonly cursor: string | null; readonly take: number },
): Promise<MemoryPage>;
```

userStories.title: Resolve proposals and restore rejected edits
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Resolve recorded save proposals at each scope's last export page and restore or remove rejected pending notes.

**Motivation** — The user ruled (2026-11-02) that nax chat and koda threads share ONE memory with koda as the source of truth, and that nax pulls a per-project mirror (pull architecture, design 6.5).

**Approach** — A `202` save means koda opened an approval request and wrote no row. If it is executed, the row appears in the export feed and a later pull replaces the mirror's pending note. If it is rejected, nothing ever appears, so the provider records each `202` save in `koda-approvals.json` in the project mirror directory.

At the last page of a pull (`done`), the provider resolves at most `MEMORY_KODA_APPROVAL_CHECKS_MAX` (20) recorded approvals of that pull's scope, oldest record first, by asking `GET approvals/<approvalId>` and reading `data.status`:

| koda status | Effect |
|---|---|
| `pending`, `approved` | kept (`approved` can still settle to `executed` or `failed`) |
| `executed` | dropped (the row arrives through the feed) |
| `rejected`, `expired`, `cancelled`, `failed` | dropped when restoration is unnecessary or succeeds; restore the slug below when eligible; keep the record if the restoring lookup throws |
| `404` | dropped; nothing restored |
| any other failure | kept; logged at warn |

**Restoring a slug.** Only when the mirror's note for that scope and slug still has `id` equal to the record's `clientId` and status `pending`, and the page has no note for that slug already, the provider calls `findActiveKodaNote` for the slug: an active row is added to the page as that slug's note (status `active`), which puts back the note an edit proposal had replaced locally; no active row adds a tombstone for the slug: the mirror's pending note itself with `status: "rejected"` (every field comes from that note, so sync's record check accepts it). A lookup that throws keeps the record (retried on a later pull) and adds nothing.

Resolving at the scope's own last page matters: sync writes a page's notes to the page's scope, so a user-scope note on a project page would land in the project mirror.

A local edit that koda answered `202` sits in the mirror as `pending` until the proposal resolves; a pull whose page carries the slug's unchanged active row (R4) replaces the pending edit with that row. The approved row arrives later through the feed. This is accepted behaviour.

Use the real createKodaApprovals to seed records, drive the provider's pull through a real HTTP client with injected fetch, and assert status/lookup requests, retained or dropped records, and returned notes. The restoring lookup is the US-006 exact-subject/scope paginated helper, not a new lookup implementation. Retain the approval on any restoring-lookup error and warn.

**Scope** — In: last-page approval resolution in koda-pull.ts and regression tests through syncMemory. Out: record format/atomic persistence (US-004), save recording (US-005), new CLI behavior (US-010/US-011). Tracking proposal forgets: a rejected proposal forget leaves the note active in koda and in the mirror, and needs no reconciliation. Keeping a pending local edit visible while its proposal is open: a pull carrying the slug's unchanged active row replaces it until the approved row arrives.

**Interface** — Extend the existing pull entry point, without changing its signature:
```typescript
export function pullKodaPage(
  input: CreateKodaMemoryProviderInput,
  request: { readonly scope: MemoryScope; readonly cursor: string | null; readonly take: number },
): Promise<MemoryPage>;
```
Use existing `KodaApprovals.list(): Promise<readonly KodaApproval[]>`, `record(entry: KodaApproval): Promise<void>`, `drop(approvalIds: readonly string[]): Promise<void>` and `MEMORY_KODA_APPROVAL_CHECKS_MAX = 20`.

[unit] A page with hasMore: true requests no approval.
[unit] A last user page requests only the approvals recorded for scope user.
[unit] A last page with 25 recorded approvals of its scope requests MEMORY_KODA_APPROVAL_CHECKS_MAX (20) of them, the oldest records first.
[unit] An approval answered pending keeps the record.
[unit] An approval answered approved keeps the record.
[unit] An approval answered executed drops the record and adds no note.
[unit] An approval answered 404 drops the record and adds no note.
[unit] An approval answered 500, or any other status-read failure except 404, keeps the record and logs a warn.
[unit] An approval answered rejected drops the record when no restoring lookup is needed or its required restoring lookup succeeds.

[unit] An approval answered failed, whose mirror note has id equal to its clientId and status pending, with no active koda row for the slug, adds to the page the mirror's pending note with status "rejected" and every other field unchanged.
[unit] An approval answered rejected, whose mirror note is pending with its clientId, with an active koda row k1 for the slug, adds k1 to the page as the slug's note with status active.
[unit] An approval answered expired whose mirror note has a different id adds no note and makes no lookup request.

**Motivation** — The user ruled (2026-11-02) that nax chat and koda threads share ONE memory with koda as the source of truth, and that nax pulls a per-project mirror (pull architecture, design 6.5).

**Approach** — `composeMemory` gains a third branch. For `provider: "koda"` it builds, through `_memoryHostDeps`:

```typescript
const client = _memoryHostDeps.createKodaClient({ url, headers, timeoutMs: MEMORY_KODA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS });
```

userStories.title: Link repositories to koda projects
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add nax memory link with safe raw-config persistence, credentialed project probing and guarded forced relinking.

**Motivation** — Today a note saved in nax chat or a `nax run` lives only in one machine's mirror (`local`) or in an MCP server that koda cannot read.

**Approach** — `nax memory link <koda-project> [-d <dir>] [--force] [--json]`, in this order:

1. `<koda-project>` failing `KODA_PROJECT_SLUG_RE` → stderr `[memory] "<koda-project>" is not a koda project slug`, exit 1, nothing written.
2. Resolves the repo root with `deps.findProjectDir` and reads `<repoRoot>/.nax/config.json` through `_memoryAdminDeps.readText` BEFORE loading the config (the loader throws on invalid project JSON first); unparsable JSON → stderr `[memory] cannot link: <path> is not valid JSON`, and JSON that is not an object (an array, `null`, a number) → stderr `[memory] cannot link: <path> is not a JSON object`; both exit 1, nothing written. Absent reads as `{}`. This parsed object is the *raw project config*.
3. Loads the merged config as the other `nax memory` subcommands do. A load error (for example a project already linked while the global `url` is missing) is reported through the existing `withMemoryErrors` path, exit 1.
4. No `memory.koda.url` in the loaded config → stderr `[memory] memory.koda.url is not set in ~/.nax/config.json`, exit 1, nothing written.
5. The raw project config already names a different `memory.koda.project` and `--force` is not set → stderr `[memory] already linked to koda project "<old>"; pass --force to relink (the project mirror is rebuilt)`, exit 1, nothing written. With `--force` (a *forced relink*: a different project is replaced), the host for the current config is opened; memory disabled (no host) skips this check and step 8; when its `status().queued + status().rejected > 0` → stderr `[memory] <n> writes are not delivered; run nax memory sync (or nax memory forget) before relinking`, exit 1, nothing written.
6. Probes `GET projects/<koda-project>/memory/write-mode` with a client built from the loaded `url` and `headers` (`MEMORY_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`); a throw, or a 2xx whose `data.mode` is not `"direct"` or `"proposal"` (the rule `reachable()` uses) → stderr `[memory] koda project "<koda-project>" is not reachable: <reason>`, exit 1, nothing written.
7. Sets `memory.provider` to `"koda"` and `memory.koda.project` to the slug **in the raw project config from step 2** — never the merged config, which holds the global `url` and `headers` — keeping every other key and value of it; writes `JSON.stringify(config, null, 2)` plus a newline through `_memoryAdminDeps.writeText` to `config.json.tmp` and `_memoryAdminDeps.rename` onto `config.json`.
8. Only a forced relink (step 5's case) then removes the host's `dirs.projectDir` through `_memoryAdminDeps.removePath`, so the next sync pulls the new project from the start (project A's export cursor would otherwise decode in project B and skip its older rows).
9. stdout `linked <repoRoot> to koda project <slug> (write mode: <mode>)`, or with `--json` one document `{ "project": "<slug>", "writeMode": "<mode>", "configPath": "<path>" }`; exit 0.

Linking the same project again rewrites the same values, needs no `--force`, and removes nothing, also when `--force` is passed. Linking a project whose config names provider `local` or `mcp` (no koda project) needs no `--force`; the notes already in the mirror stay local (Out of Scope: migration).

`registerMemoryCommand` (`src/cli/memory.ts:176`) — Target: also calls `registerMemoryAdminCommands(memory, deps)`, which adds `link` and `reset` after `approve`. This story registers only link; US-011 adds reset. Update the four existing subcommand-name assertions in memory-read.test.ts, memory-forget.test.ts, memory-save.test.ts and memory-smoke-fixes.test.ts to gain link after approve.

Tests trigger memoryLinkCommand with _kodaClientDeps.fetch, _memoryAdminDeps and the host stubbed; one case executes the command through the registered Commander program. Avoid importing shared plumbing from memory.ts and closing an import cycle. Use existing withMemoryErrors and host lifecycle cleanup for thrown failures.

**Scope** — In: memory-admin.ts link implementation, admin filesystem seam, registration and link tests. Out: reset action (US-011), global-only guard (US-012), host/provider algorithms (US-005–US-009). Resetting the user mirror: `nax memory reset` and a forced relink remove project mirror files only. Guarding `nax memory reset` or a forced `nax memory link` against another nax process using the same mirror at the same time. Preserving comments or formatting in `.nax/config.json` when `nax memory link` rewrites it (the file is plain JSON, rewritten with two-space indentation). Migrating notes already in a `local` or `mcp` mirror into koda when a project is first linked: they stay in the mirror and are not pushed. Inferring the koda project from the git remote; `nax memory link` takes the slug as an argument. Approval records after a forced relink: the relink removes `koda-approvals.json` with the rest of the project mirror (the approvals belong to the old koda project), so a user-scope note pending in the old project stays `pending` in the user mirror until forgotten.

**Interface** —
```typescript
export const _memoryAdminDeps: {
  readText(path: string): Promise<string | null>;          // null when the file does not exist
  writeText(path: string, text: string): Promise<void>;    // creates parent directories
  rename(from: string, to: string): Promise<void>;
  listDir(path: string): Promise<readonly string[]>;       // entry names; [] when the directory does not exist
  removePath(path: string): Promise<void>;                 // recursive; a missing path is not an error
```

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add nax memory reset with provider/delivery guards, approval preservation and outcome-sensitive resync.

**Motivation** — The user ruled (2026-11-02) that nax chat and koda threads share ONE memory with koda as the source of truth, and that nax pulls a per-project mirror (pull architecture, design 6.5).

**Approach** — `nax memory reset [-d <dir>] [--json]`:

1. Opens the host as the other subcommands do; memory disabled keeps the existing disabled error (`memoryDisabledError`) and exit code.
2. A provider id not starting with `koda:` → stderr `[memory] reset needs memory.provider "koda": the <provider id> mirror is the only copy of its notes`, exit 1, nothing deleted.
3. `status().queued + status().rejected > 0` → stderr `[memory] <n> writes are not delivered; run nax memory sync (or nax memory forget) before reset`, exit 1, nothing deleted.
4. Removes every entry `_memoryAdminDeps.listDir` lists in the host's `dirs.projectDir`, through `_memoryAdminDeps.removePath`, except `koda-approvals.json` (records of proposals still pending in koda, including user-scope ones whose notes live in the untouched user mirror), then runs `host.sync()` and prints its result exactly as `nax memory sync` does (`formatMemorySyncResult`, or one JSON document with `--json`).
5. Exit `0` when the sync outcome is `"synced"`, else `1` (an `unreachable` reset leaves an empty mirror, which the user must hear about).

Add memoryResetCommand to memory-admin.ts and register reset after link. Update memory-read.test.ts, memory-forget.test.ts, memory-save.test.ts and memory-smoke-fixes.test.ts registration-name assertions to gain reset after link. Use the existing filesystem seam created by US-010; listDir answers entry names and [] for a missing directory, removePath is recursive and tolerates missing paths. Preserve koda-approvals.json bytes by never deleting or rewriting it in the reset phase. Join listed entries beneath dirs.projectDir, not userDir or the mirror root. Reuse formatting, not memorySyncCommand's exit rule: ordinary sync treats unreachable/locked as exit 0, but reset must report every non-synced outcome as exit 1.

Tests trigger memoryResetCommand with _memoryAdminDeps and host stubbed, assert guards/deletion order/preserved bytes/results, and run the subcommand through the registered Commander program. Keep the shared host lifecycle and error contract.

**Scope** — In: reset action, admin registration and reset tests. Out: link behavior (US-010), provider pull/approval algorithms (US-007/US-008), changes to ordinary sync exit behavior. Resetting the user mirror: `nax memory reset` and a forced relink remove project mirror files only. Guarding `nax memory reset` or a forced `nax memory link` against another nax process using the same mirror at the same time.

**Interface** —
```typescript
export function memoryResetCommand(opts: MemoryCliOptions, deps?: MemoryCliDeps): Promise<number>;
export function registerMemoryAdminCommands(memory: Command, deps?: MemoryCliDeps): Command;
```
Use the existing `_memoryAdminDeps` readText/writeText/rename/listDir/removePath contract without replacing the seam object.

No koda repository changes, package version changes, new dependencies, or nax-agent API changes are needed.

Architecture and conventions: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:151-159 documents the 600-line hard source limit, 800-line hard test limit, short functions, named constants, stage-prefixed NaxError and injectable _deps for external operations. packages/nax/package.json:49 defines the wrapped test runner, :55 the targeted unit command, and :80 the check:all gate. Config impact: packages/nax/src/config/schemas-memory.ts:65 currently accepts only local/mcp; :96 memoryConfigOf is the defaults accessor; :102 defines the partially checked cross-section input; :121 implements four independent MCP validations. Retain those rules and defaults while adding an optional strict koda block and independent missing-url/missing-project issues. packages/nax/src/config/schemas.ts:528 owns the memory default and :594 invokes validateMemoryProvider, so no second schema/default source is needed. packages/nax/src/config/runtime-types-memory.ts:32 is the handwritten MemoryConfig union and must stay aligned with the schema. packages/nax/src/config/index.ts:56 and :141-149 are the export sites. packages/nax/src/config/schemas-model.ts:184 exposes isRemotePlainHttp with loopback exceptions declared at :179; reuse it, rather than inventing another host classifier. packages/nax/test/unit/config/schemas-memory.test.ts:47 and :293 deliberately reject koda today and must be replaced, not left as contradictory regressions; :240 pins the existing MCP proposal refusal, which stays.

Credentials and layer trust: packages/nax/src/config/global-only-keys.ts:6 currently rejects trust/auth and returns its input. Extend it to reject nested memory.koda.url and headers whenever set in a non-global layer, including empty header maps. Existing call sites cover project (loader.ts:139), CLI (:197), package (:346 and :461), and profile (profile.ts:112); do not add a second layer policy. Existing tests include test/unit/config/global-only-keys.test.ts:83 and loader-auth-global-only.test.ts. The header masker at packages/nax/src/cli/config-profile.ts:147-175 already masks every value of any headers map, including Authorization, so no masking change is required. packages/nax/src/cli/config-descriptions.ts:455-475 is the memory descriptions block; it currently mentions only local/mcp. Credentials remain literal global headers; preserve opaque values and never emit them into transport errors, context, logs, or generated project config. A remote HTTP API is rejected because credentials travel with every request.

Provider contract: packages/nax-agent/src/memory/provider-types.ts:14-45 supplies MemoryWriteRequest, MemoryPushResult, MemoryPage, and MemoryProvider. Its error contract (:8-10) makes only MEMORY_PUSH_REJECTED permanent; other throws remain queued. MemoryNote/MemoryDecision/MemoryHit and vocabulary/limits are in packages/nax-agent/src/memory/types.ts:9-73 and :88-110. The public entry supplies the types, MEMORY_SLUG_RE, MEMORY_SOURCE_MAX_CHARS, MEMORY_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS=2000 and MEMORY_OP_TIMEOUT_MS=10000, but not MEMORY_NOTE_TYPES; declare the typed KODA_NOTE_TYPES locally, as NOTE_TYPES does in packages/nax/src/cli/memory-cli-deps.ts:40. The new HTTP client is a small injected fetch adapter, not an MCP client or LLM client. projects/<slug> routes use the project slug; save/retire bodies use a memoised string project id from GET projects/<slug>. Clear failed project-id attempts rather than caching invalid results. Reachability must probe the project write-mode route, not health, because membership matters. koda owns write mode: do not send request.writeMode, and map 201/202 independently of local writeMode. sourceId=clientId provides identical-restatement replay safety, not a general idempotency API.

Existing implementation patterns: packages/nax/src/memory/mcp-provider.ts:44 defines the permanent rejection pattern and :51-159 implements the existing remote provider. packages/nax/src/plugins/builtin/reporter-shared/post-json.ts:9 is an injectable fetch seam and :48-77 demonstrates header-safe transport logging, but its swallow-on-error semantics are not the new client's contract. packages/nax/src/memory/mcp-id-map.ts:51 provides file seams, :109-123 uses temporary-file-plus-rename, and :132-165 serialises mutations and rereads disk. Follow this persistence style for versioned koda-approvals.json, preserving record order and replacing by (scope, slug). Invalid/unreadable approval files warn once per instance and read as empty. Unlike MCP ids, koda approvals for both scopes live in the PROJECT mirror directory.

Pull correctness is the highest-risk algorithm: packages/nax-agent/src/memory/sync.ts:316-340 applies each page by slug, not by remote id; :332-333 deletes a tombstoned slug unconditionally. Therefore a raw stale predecessor tombstone can erase a newer note unless the provider reconciles each feed page first. Read distinct valid NOTE slug ids from the mirror before reconciling. Apply R1-R6 in feed order, with separate unknown-current-id state after a matching superseded predecessor, emit at most one note per slug in code-point order, and never persist page-local reconciliation state across pages. packages/nax-agent/src/memory/sync.ts:355-369 checkpoint each applied page and retain the previous cursor when a pull fails. Each scope has an independent cursor although koda returns a combined feed with no scope query. Validate items array and boolean hasMore before returning a page. User pages must not return decisions or project approval resolutions. Merge DECISION rows by id only on project pages, rereading decisions between pages, sorting updatedAt descending then id, limiting to 500, and returning undefined when no valid decision rows occur. packages/nax-agent/src/memory/store.ts:141-146 exposes the required reads and writeDecisions; do not modify it. Note/decision row validation skips malformed records and emits one counted warn per page. Existing mcp-results.ts:41-83 is a parser pattern, not the target koda wire format.

Proposal lifecycle: a 202 save writes no koda row, so recording approvalId/scope/slug/clientId is necessary to resolve rejection. Resolve at most 20 oldest same-scope approvals only on that scope's last page. Pending/approved remain, executed/404 drop without restoration, terminal rejected/expired/cancelled/failed drop only after any required restoring lookup succeeds. Restore only a still-pending mirror note whose id matches clientId and whose slug is absent from the page: use the exact active remote row, or the entire pending note with status rejected as the tombstone. A failed restoring lookup keeps the record and warns. koda's five-second settle window means executed may drop before the row appears; eventual feed delivery is intended. An unchanged active row may overwrite a pending edit before proposal resolution; do not attempt to preserve that edit. The lookup uses a prefix subject query but must verify exact subject and scope, paginate up to ten pages, and treat lookup/project lookup failures as transient; only the RETIRE request maps 404/409 to deleted.

Add a third branch using the same store/outbox, no new runtime resource owner, and fail on bypassed missing koda config at creation. :377-383 already provides no-op idempotent close without a pool; :466-498 exposes the unchanged host API. packages/nax/src/memory/host-remote-search.ts:27-57 already invokes provider.search for project/unscoped requests, catches failures with one warn, and :63-72 merges remote hits before local slugs; do not modify it to add user remote search. packages/nax/src/memory/index.ts:8-20 is the barrel to extend. Existing test/unit/memory/host-mcp.test.ts:100-128 demonstrates temp global-dir isolation, factory stubs and restoration; use it to test the new branch, plus real-client/store integration. Consumers remain compatible: src/cli/chat.ts:30, src/chat/host-memory.ts:26, src/chat/resources.ts:2, src/tui/chat/slash-commands.ts:17, and src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup.ts:36 import the host/barrel and need no feature changes.

CLI integration: packages/nax/src/cli/memory.ts:116 reports status via host.status and :176-199 registers read/write groups; register the new admin group afterward so link/reset follow approve. packages/nax/src/cli/memory-cli-deps.ts:63-72 defines MemoryCliDeps, :161-165 resolves root/config, :193-213 closes hosts in finally, and :236-243 translates thrown errors to Error: <message> and exit 1. Link has a special ordering constraint: validate slug, resolve root and parse raw project JSON BEFORE merged-config load, then check url/relink queue, probe, atomically rewrite only raw project data, and only afterward delete the old project mirror for a forced DIFFERENT-project relink. Loading merged config before parsing would lose the required invalid-JSON message. Persisting merged data would leak global URL/headers and violate US-012. A disabled current host skips queue/removal steps, but not the new project's probe/config write. Same-project linking, even with force, never clears anything. Link from local/mcp preserves existing mirror notes and performs no migration.

Reset must preserve koda-approvals.json byte-for-byte and never touch userDir. Reject non-koda ids and any queued/rejected writes before deletion; remove only entries listed under projectDir, then sync once. packages/nax/src/cli/memory-read.ts:74-84 formats sync output but normally exits 0 for unreachable/locked; reset intentionally differs and exits 0 ONLY for synced. test/unit/cli/memory-read.test.ts:262 pins disabled errors, :269 locks the existing locked exit behavior, and :293-309 asserts registration names.
